generic_domain.justification: Graph Neural Networks is the most general domain as it forms the foundation for various applications, including node classification, link prediction, and more. It underpins other specific domains like Graph Representation Learning, which focuses on how nodes and edges are represented in lower-dimensional spaces, often using techniques that are subsets of GNNs. Similarly, Graph-based Deep generative Models like GraphGAN or GraphVAE build upon the principles established by GNNs to generate synthetic graphs. Temporal Graph Neural Networks extend traditional GNNs to handle dynamic graph data over time, and Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks address complex real-world scenarios with diverse node types. Therefore, GNN serves as a comprehensive umbrella under which these specialized domains operate.
